texts.value: Proofreading amidase that contributes to the maintenance of cell wall composition and integrity (PubMed:28612943, PubMed:35164571, PubMed:40632566). It prevents the mis-incorporation of both L-serine and glycine containing precursors into the peptidoglycan (PG) sacculi (PubMed:28612943, PubMed:35164571, PubMed:40632566). Acts by hydrolyzing UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-serine (UDP-MurNAc-L-Ser) to release L-serine and UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-glycine (UDP-MurNAc-Gly) to release glycine, thereby preventing the mis-incorporation of these amino acids into the PG and ensuring that only the correct PG precursor, UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala, is incorporated (PubMed:35164571, PubMed:40632566). It can also use UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala, with 10-fold lower activity compared to UDP-MurNAc-L-Ser, and it exhibits weak activity toward UDP-MurNAc-L-Ala-D-Glu (UMAE) and UDP-MurNAc-L-Ser-D-Glu (UMSE) (PubMed:35164571). It does not exhibit PG hydrolytic activity (PubMed:28612943)

The enzyme also shows purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) activity in vitro (PubMed:31978345). It can catalyze the phosphorolysis of adenosine and inosine nucleosides, yielding D-ribose 1-phosphate and the respective free bases, adenine and hypoxanthine (PubMed:31978345). However, this PNP activity is weak, requires higher protein concentration as compared to the precursor editing activity, and cannot confer growth to a PNP-deficient mutant in vivo, suggesting that it may not be physiologically significant in E.coli (PubMed:40632566). In addition, the enzyme has several other activities in vitro: it can catalyze the phosphorolysis of S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine into adenine and S-methyl-5-thio-alpha-D-ribose 1-phosphate, and it has adenosine deaminase activity (PubMed:31978345). It also shows polyphenol oxidase activity and is able to oxidize syringaldazine and 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzthiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) (ABTS) (PubMed:16740638)

Was originally thought to be periplasmic, but the presence of the N-terminal region in the structure indicates that PgeF does not possess a signal peptide and therefore is a cytoplasmic protein (PubMed:28612943, PubMed:35164571). It was subsequently confirmed that it is located in the cytoplasm (PubMed:40632566)

The mutant shows incorporation of L-serine or glycine in place of L-alanine in peptidoglycan (PubMed:28612943, PubMed:40632566). It also shows altered cell morphology and reduced peptidoglycan synthesis (PubMed:28612943). Cells lacking this gene are more sensitive to ampicillin, cephradine and cefoxitin than wild-type strain (PubMed:20065048). The deletion mutant is extremely sensitive to cephalexin and ampicillin and weakly susceptible to other classes of beta-lactam antibiotics, which affect cell wall biosynthesis (PubMed:28612943). It is not susceptible to any of the antibiotics affecting other cellular processes or to outer membrane disrupting agents (PubMed:28612943). All phenotypes of the mutant can be suppressed by a decrease in the intracellular pool of L-serine/glycine (PubMed:28612943). The phenotypes of the mutant are fully complemented by homologs from S.enterica, B.subtilis or G.stearothermophilus (PubMed:40632566)
Peptidoglycan editing and PNP activities of PgeF proceed through distinct and independent catalytic mechanisms
